title: Explanation-based Finetuning Makes Models More Robust to Spurious Cues

bias_targets.methodology: Artificially skewing training datasets so that non-causal structural or lexical features (e.g., sentence length, verb tense, plural nouns, username mentions, perplexity, and K-means embedding clusters) perfectly correlate with a target label, and then measuring the model's reliance on these features on an unskewed test set using accuracy drop and the Matthews correlation coefficient.

bias_targets.target: Gender bias (evaluated as a dataset artifact)
bias_targets.methodology: Introducing a domain-specific spurious cue in the e-SNLI dataset where female-related words and pronouns (e.g., 'woman', 'girl', 'lady') are artificially perfectly correlated with a target label, and evaluating the model's predictive correlation with this gendered cue to see if it learns the demographic shortcut.
